steps.description: Mark it out in one four-by-eight bed. (1) Tomato: 4 plants — 2–3 ft apart, staked or caged; fewer plants, better fruit. (2) Lettuce: 24 row-feet — three 8 ft rows, cut-and-come-again. (3) Kale: 6 plants — 18 in apart; it keeps giving until the ground freezes. (4) Bush bean: 16 row-feet — two 8 ft rows, seed 3–4 in apart. (5) Cherry tomato: 3 plants — 3 ft apart and give them a tall stake — they get big.
steps.wateringNeeds: Deep soak twice a week; keep leaves dry to slow blight.

steps.description: Sheet-mulch the paths and any new ground this fall — cardboard, then compost, then whatever the town will give you. Skip the tiller; the worms do the work.
One soaker line down the middle of the tomato bed. Deep and infrequent beats a daily sprinkle. Deep soak twice a week; keep leaves dry to slow blight.
steps.wateringNeeds: Deep soak twice a week; keep leaves dry to slow blight.

steps.description: Support before you plant, not after: tomato and cherry tomato need stakes, cages or a trellis on day one. Then a cold frame at one end for the lettuce — hinge it south, reuse a storm window.
Sow the lettuce every 14 days from a week after last frost — that stagger is what keeps one impossible week from eating the whole harvest.
steps.wateringNeeds: Deep soak twice a week; keep leaves dry to slow blight.
